answer: Tie each agent to an authenticated satellite position. Its host must run a GNSS receiver that checks Galileo OSNMA signatures, so spoofed fixes fail, and the network allows one agent per 100 m cell. A hobbyist on a rooftop terrace and a lab by a coral reef each count once. A farm whose clones claim distinct cells but answer from one machine shows a tight spiral of drifting fixes and matching clocks, and is pruned. Faking 200 real sites at about $50 a month each costs roughly $10,000 monthly.
